name: TN Smart Ration Card (TNPDS)
department: Civil Supplies and Consumer Protection Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
introduced: The shift from paper ration cards to digital Smart Cards was announced in 2018 under then Chief Minister Edappadi K. Palanisamy, as part of the Tamil Nadu Public Distribution System (TNPDS) modernisation.
summary: A digital, Aadhaar-linked ration card that replaces the old paper book. No physical card is needed — you're verified by biometrics at your local ration shop.
about: The Smart Ration Card is used to buy subsidised rice, wheat, sugar, kerosene and other essential commodities from your assigned Fair Price Shop every month. It also doubles as a widely accepted proof of identity and address.
eligibility_text: Open to all Tamil Nadu households. Your category — Priority Household (PHH) or Non-Priority Household (NPHH) — depends on your family's income and situation, and determines exactly what you can buy at subsidised rates.
documents_required: Aadhaar card of the head of family and all family members
Proof of address (electricity bill, rental agreement, property tax receipt, or voter ID)
Proof of income (salary slip, income certificate from Tahsildar, or self-declaration)
Passport-size photo of the family head
how_to_apply: Apply online at tnpds.gov.in/register-a-card, or offline at your nearest Taluk Supply Office, Revenue Office, or e-Sevai centre.

name: Community Certificate (Caste Certificate)
department: Revenue Department, Government of Tamil Nadu (issued by Tahsildar / Deputy Tahsildar)
introduced: A long-standing Revenue Department administrative service rather than a scheme with a single launch date — it moved onto the e-Sevai digital portal as part of TNeGA's e-governance rollout.
status: Active — issued on an ongoing basis
summary: An official certificate confirming you belong to a specific community category (SC / ST / MBC / DNT / OBC). Once issued, it's valid for your lifetime.
about: This certificate is required to access reservation benefits in education, government jobs, and many welfare schemes that are tiered by community category.
eligibility_text: You must belong to a recognised reserved category, be an Indian citizen residing in Tamil Nadu, and be at least 3 years old.
documents_required: Parents' identity proof and affidavit (if applicant is a minor)
how_to_apply: Apply online through an e-Sevai / Common Service Centre, or offline at your local ward office or Tahsildar's office.
fee: Not specified by source — verify at time of application
processing_time: Within 15 days for General/BC/MBC categories; up to 30 days for Scheduled Tribes
helpline: Contact your local Tahsildar office or e-Sevai centre

name: Old Age Pension (Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme – TN)
department: Department of Social Welfare and Women Empowerment, Government of Tamil Nadu
introduced: Tamil Nadu's old-age pension system dates back decades as part of the state's long-running Social Security Schemes; the current scheme runs jointly with the central Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS). We haven't pinned down a single original launch year/CM for this one — flagging that honestly rather than guessing.
summary: A monthly pension for destitute elderly residents with no other means of support.
about: Provides ₹1,000 per month to elderly people who are destitute, below the poverty line, and have no one else to depend on for support.
eligibility_text: Age 60 or above; destitute and unable to work; below poverty line; assets under ₹50,000; no relative aged 18+ capable of supporting you.
documents_required: BPL certificate (from Corporation office in urban areas, or BDO/Panchayat office in rural areas)
how_to_apply: Apply at your area's Village Administrative Officer (VAO) office, Taluk Office, or e-Sevai centre.
processing_time: Varies by district — check with your local Taluk office
helpline: Contact your local Taluk Social Welfare office

name: Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme (CMCHIS)
department: Health & Family Welfare Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
introduced: Originally launched in 2009 as ‘Kalaignar Kaappittu Thittam’ under M. Karunanidhi, renamed CMCHIS in 2012. Coverage was raised from ₹5 lakh to ₹25 lakh per family per year in August 2026 under the current government.
summary: Free health insurance covering hospital treatment for eligible low-income families, currently up to ₹25 lakh per family per year.
about: Covers a wide range of medical and surgical procedures at network hospitals across Tamil Nadu, with cashless treatment for eligible families.
eligibility_text: Annual family income below ₹1,20,000. (If your income is above this, you likely won't qualify for CMCHIS specifically — but keep this on file, as thresholds are occasionally revised.)
how_to_apply: Register at your nearest network hospital, government hospital, or CMCHIS help desk with your ration card and Aadhaar.
processing_time: Cards typically issued within a few weeks of registration
helpline: Check cmchistn.com for the current helpline number

name: Chief Minister's Uzhavar Pathukappu Thittam (Farmers' Welfare Scheme)
department: Commissionerate of Revenue Administration, Government of Tamil Nadu
introduced: The official portal identifies this scheme with the year 2011, suggesting that's when it was established or last revamped — we haven't independently confirmed the exact launch date or founding Chief Minister from a primary announcement, so treat that year as indicative rather than certain.
status: Active — over 1.47 crore registered farmer members
summary: A welfare board for farmers and agricultural workers that pays out for old age, accidents, death, marriage, and children's education — separate from crop subsidies.
about: This is a social security net for agricultural workers, not a crop or land subsidy. Registered members and their dependents can claim a range of benefits: old age pension, accident and natural death assistance, marriage assistance, and education support for children, funded through the welfare board.
eligibility_text: Open to agricultural labourers and farmers who register as members with the welfare board — you don't need to own large landholdings to join. Different benefits (pension, accident relief, marriage assistance, education support) have their own specific conditions once you're a registered member.
documents_required: Proof of agricultural occupation / land or labour records
Registration form for the welfare board
how_to_apply: Register through the official CMUPT portal (oap.tn.gov.in/cmupt) or at your local Revenue/Taluk office; specific benefit claims (pension, accident, marriage, education) are filed separately once you're a registered member. Note: the Revenue Department's official page for this scheme has been observed to load unreliably (it can show a 'File not found' error even though it's the correct, legitimate link) — if that happens, try again after a few minutes, or visit your nearest Taluk/Revenue office directly to enrol or check your status.
fee: Not specified by source — verify at registration
helpline: Contact your local Taluk Revenue office
benefit_highlights: Children's education support: ₹1,250 – ₹6,750/year depending on course level

name: Micro Irrigation (Drip & Sprinkler) Subsidy
department: Agricultural Engineering Department / Directorate of Horticulture and Plantation Crops, Government of Tamil Nadu
introduced: Implemented in Tamil Nadu as the state component of the central Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) – Per Drop More Crop, a national scheme; run locally by the Agricultural Engineering Department and Directorate of Horticulture.
summary: Government-funded drip and sprinkler irrigation equipment for your farm — up to 100% subsidised for small and marginal farmers.
about: Covers the cost of installing drip or sprinkler irrigation systems, which use water far more efficiently than flood irrigation. Small and marginal farmers (typically those with landholdings up to about 5 acres) receive the highest subsidy rate.
eligibility_text: Farmers with cultivable land, roughly in the 0.5 to 5 acre range for the highest (up to 100%) subsidy tier; larger holdings can still apply but at a lower subsidy percentage.
documents_required: Aadhaar card and a photo ID
Field map / topo sketch of the land
Quotation from an approved micro-irrigation company
Signed agreement not to transfer the equipment for 3 years
how_to_apply: Apply online via the PMKSY portal (select the Horticulture department, fill in Aadhaar and bank details, upload documents), or offline through your Agricultural Officer with a Subsidy Requisition Application, certified by the Assistant Agricultural Officer and submitted to the Directorate of Horticulture office.
fee: None — cost is subsidised, remainder paid by farmer
processing_time: Not specified by source — varies by district and equipment vendor
helpline: Directorate of Horticulture and Plantation Crops, Chennai

name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) — Crop Insurance
department: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (Government of India), implemented in Tamil Nadu via the Agriculture Department and empanelled insurers
introduced: Launched nationally on 18 February 2016 by the Government of India; enrollment became fully voluntary (rather than compulsory for loanee farmers) from the 2020 Kharif season onward.
summary: Low-cost crop insurance — you pay a small fixed share of the premium, and the government covers the rest, protecting you against crop loss from natural causes.
about: Insures your crop against yield loss from natural calamities, pests, and diseases. The farmer's premium share is capped by crop type, with the government subsidising the remaining actuarial premium.
eligibility_text: Any farmer growing a notified crop in a notified area for that season can enrol — including tenant farmers and sharecroppers, not just landowners. Your premium share is capped at 2% for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi food/oilseed crops, and 5% for commercial/horticultural crops. Note: perennial plantation/tree crops like coconut and arecanut are generally not covered under PMFBY — they have their own dedicated insurance (e.g. the Coconut Palm Insurance Scheme) instead.
documents_required: Land ownership proof or land records
Tenant/sharecropper certificate (if you don't own the land)
Bank account passbook (name must match Aadhaar exactly)
how_to_apply: Enrol through the PMFBY portal, your bank (if you have a crop loan), a Common Service Centre (CSC), or your local Agriculture Department office — before the season's cut-off date, which varies by crop and district.
fee: Farmer pays a capped premium share (2% Kharif / 1.5% Rabi / 5% commercial-horticultural); government subsidises the rest
processing_time: Enrollment must be completed before the season's notified cut-off date

name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC)
department: Available through nationalised banks, cooperative banks, and regional rural banks (including Tamil Nadu Grama Bank)
introduced: A long-running central government credit scheme for farmers, introduced in the late 1990s and enhanced since with interest subvention benefits.
summary: An easy-access credit line for farming needs, with government interest support that can bring your effective rate down to around 4% for loans up to ₹3 lakh if repaid on time.
about: Works like a revolving cash-credit account sized to your cropping pattern and land — no need to reapply for a fresh loan every season. Covers crop production costs and can extend to post-harvest and allied needs.
eligibility_text: Owner-cultivators, tenant farmers, oral lessees, and sharecroppers are all eligible, individually or as a group — you do not need to own the land.
documents_required: Revenue-certified proof of landholding (or tenancy/lease proof)
Details of crops grown and acreage
Security documents (only required for loans above ₹1.6–2 lakh)
how_to_apply: Apply at any nationalised bank, cooperative bank, or regional rural bank branch — application forms are also available on most banks' agricultural banking portals.
fee: No processing fee for loans up to ₹3 lakh; small percentage fee above that
helpline: Contact your nearest bank branch's agricultural banking desk

name: Post-Matric Scholarship for SC/ST Students
department: Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
introduced: A long-running central-and-state scheme administered by the Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department — we haven't verified a specific single launch year or Chief Minister for the current Tamil Nadu implementation.
summary: Covers 100% of tuition and compulsory fees for SC/ST students from Class 11 through PhD, plus a monthly maintenance allowance.
about: Reimburses tuition and compulsory non-refundable fees in full, and pays a monthly allowance (₹250–₹1,200 depending on course and hostel status via Direct Benefit Transfer). Fees at private institutions are capped at ₹1 lakh/year, and students with disabilities get an extra 10% allowance.
eligibility_text: SC, ST, SCA or SCC student, Tamil Nadu resident, from Class 11 onward (including UG, PG, diploma, ITI, and PhD across all streams). Annual family income must not exceed ₹2.5 lakh.
documents_required: Aadhaar card with linked bank account
how_to_apply: Complete One Time Registration (OTR) on the National Scholarship Portal or Tamil Nadu State Scholarship Portal using Aadhaar, log in, select the SC/ST Post-Matric scheme, fill in your details, upload documents, and submit before the deadline (typically 30 November).
processing_time: Processed after the annual application window closes
helpline: Contact your Adi Dravidar Welfare district office

name: Pre-Matric Scholarship (BC/MBC/DNC, Classes 6–10)
department: Backward Classes Welfare Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
introduced: Long-running Backward Classes Welfare Department scheme — specific launch year not verified from available sources.
summary: Waives tuition, special, and exam fees for BC/MBC/DNC students in government schools, Classes 6 through 10.
about: Covers school fees directly rather than paying cash to the student — the waiver is applied by the school itself for eligible students.
eligibility_text: BC, MBC, or DNC student in Classes 6–10 at a government school; annual family income up to ₹2.5 lakh.
how_to_apply: No separate application needed in most cases — implemented directly through your school. Check with your school's headmaster or the local Backward Classes Welfare office.
helpline: Your school office, or the local BC/MBC/DNC Welfare office

name: Post-Matric Scholarship (BC/MBC/DNC, Classes 11–12)
department: Backward Classes Welfare Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
introduced: Long-running Backward Classes Welfare Department scheme — specific launch year not verified from available sources.
summary: Covers examination fees for BC/MBC/DNC students in Classes 11 and 12 — income limit is waived entirely for MBC/DNC students.
about: A smaller, targeted scheme that removes the exam-fee barrier for higher secondary students, on top of any tuition-fee waivers already in place at government schools.
eligibility_text: BC, MBC, or DNC student in Class 11 or 12. Income limit of ₹2.5 lakh applies to BC students; MBC/DNC students have no income limit for this scheme.
how_to_apply: Applied through your school — check with your headmaster or local Backward Classes Welfare office.
processing_time: Applied each academic year around exam registration
helpline: Your school office, or the local BC/MBC/DNC Welfare office

name: Post-Matric Scholarship (BC/MBC/DNC, College Level)
department: Backward Classes Welfare Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
introduced: Long-running Backward Classes Welfare Department scheme — specific launch year not verified from available sources.
summary: Covers tuition, special and exam fees, book money, and a hostel allowance for BC/MBC/DNC students in ITI, diploma, UG, PG, professional, or PhD courses.
about: One of the broadest BC/MBC/DNC support schemes — covers most of the direct cost of college beyond living expenses, plus ₹400/month if you're staying in a hostel.
eligibility_text: BC, MBC, or DNC student in ITI, diploma, undergraduate, postgraduate, professional, or PhD courses. Income limit of ₹2.5 lakh applies to BC students; MBC/DNC students generally have no income limit.
documents_required: Bonafide certificate and marksheets from your institution
how_to_apply: Apply through the Unified State Scholarship Portal (umis.tn.gov.in) using your Aadhaar and UMIS ID from your institution.
processing_time: Processed after the annual application window closes

name: PM-YASASVI Post-Matric Scholarship
department: Central scheme (Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment), implemented in Tamil Nadu via the Backward Classes Welfare Department
introduced: A central government scheme (Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment) implemented alongside Tamil Nadu's own BC/MBC/DNC schemes.
summary: Covers full tuition, fees, and book money for OBC/DNC students in undergraduate, polytechnic, or professional courses.
about: Runs alongside the state's own post-matric scheme, aimed at OBC and DNC students specifically, with slightly different documentation (a national entrance test, YET, decides some award tiers).
eligibility_text: OBC or DNC student in an undergraduate, polytechnic, or professional course; income limit generally ₹2.5 lakh, varying by course type.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Unified State Scholarship Portal (USSP) with your Aadhaar-linked bank account.
processing_time: Processed after the annual application window closes

name: Scholarship for BC/MBC/DNC Students at IIT/IIM/NIT/Central Universities
department: Backward Classes Welfare Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
introduced: Long-running Backward Classes Welfare Department scheme — specific launch year not verified from available sources.
summary: Up to ₹2 lakh per year for BC/MBC/DNC students admitted to premier institutions like IITs, IIMs, NITs, or central universities.
about: A higher-value top-up scheme specifically for students who get into premier national institutions, covering tuition and fees that the state's standard scholarship amount wouldn't fully cover.
eligibility_text: BC, MBC, or DNC student pursuing UG or PG studies at an IIT, IIM, NIT, or central university; annual family income up to ₹2.5 lakh.
how_to_apply: Submit forms directly to the Backward Classes Welfare Directorate with your institution's endorsement.
helpline: Directorate of Backward Classes Welfare, Chennai

disability: A parent of mine has a certified disability

name: Scholarship for Sons/Daughters of Differently Abled Persons
department: Department of Welfare of Differently Abled Persons, Government of Tamil Nadu
introduced: Long-running scheme under the Department of Welfare of Differently Abled Persons — specific launch year not verified from available sources.
summary: An annual scholarship for students whose parent holds a valid Differently Abled Welfare Board ID card — from Class 11 through postgraduate study.
about: A modest but genuinely useful annual payment (₹1,000–₹6,000 depending on education level and hostel status) that many eligible families don't know exists, since it's tied to the parent's disability status rather than the student's own.
eligibility_text: Your parent holds a valid Tamil Nadu Differently Abled Welfare Board ID card; you're enrolled in Class 11 through postgraduate study (including ITI/polytechnic) and passed your previous class.
how_to_apply: Download the application form from your District Differently Abled Welfare office's page, complete it, and submit to your District Differently Abled Welfare Officer.
processing_time: Funds transfer annually to the student's joint account after approval
helpline: Your District Differently Abled Welfare Officer

name: Coconut Palm Insurance Scheme (CPIS)
department: Coconut Development Board, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (Government of India), with State Government premium support
introduced: Run by the Coconut Development Board (established 12 January 1981). The exact year CPIS itself was launched could not be independently confirmed from the sources checked — treat it as an established, long-running CDB scheme rather than a new one.
summary: Low-cost insurance for your coconut or arecanut palms against storms, drought, pests, fire, earthquake, tsunami and landslide damage — you pay only a small fraction of the premium.
about: Insures individual coconut palms (a minimum of 5 healthy, nut-bearing palms in one contiguous plot) against major natural and calamity-related risks. Premiums are heavily subsidised: the Coconut Development Board covers 50%, the State Government covers 25%, leaving the grower to pay the remaining 25% (or as little as 10% where the state adds a higher share).
eligibility_text: You need a minimum of 5 healthy, nut-bearing palms in a contiguous area. Dwarf/hybrid palm varieties must be aged 4–60 years; tall palm varieties 7–60 years. Partial insurance of a plantation (insuring only some palms in one contiguous block) is not allowed — the full eligible block must be covered.
documents_required: Proof of land ownership or cultivation rights
Palm count and age declaration for the plot
Bank account passbook (for premium payment / any claim payout)
how_to_apply: Enrol through the Coconut Development Board's regional office, the State Horticulture/Agriculture Department, or the implementing insurance agency, generally by 31 March each year (later enrolment is possible, with coverage starting from the 1st of the following month). Contact your nearest CDB regional office or Horticulture Department office to confirm the current enrolment window and implementing agency in your district.
fee: ₹9 per palm/year (ages 4–15, sum insured ₹900) or ₹14 per palm/year (ages 16–60, sum insured ₹1,750) — and that's already after the 50% CDB + 25% state subsidy, so this is roughly your actual out-of-pocket share, not the full premium.
processing_time: Coverage begins on the 1st of the month following successful enrolment and premium payment
helpline: Nearest Coconut Development Board regional office, or your district's Horticulture/Agriculture Department office

name: Rashtriya Gokul Mission — Free Artificial Insemination for Cattle
department: Department of Animal Husbandry, Government of Tamil Nadu, with Tamil Nadu Cooperative Milk Producers' Federation and TANUVAS, under the central Rashtriya Gokul Mission
introduced: Rashtriya Gokul Mission was launched nationally by the Government of India in December 2014 to improve indigenous cattle breeds; Tamil Nadu's own district-wise rollout date under TNLDA is not independently confirmed.
summary: Free doorstep artificial insemination for your cattle, with an optional sex-sorted semen option that gives an 85%+ chance of a female calf — useful if you're building up a dairy herd.
about: Provides free bovine artificial insemination (AI) at the farmer's doorstep, using high genetic merit bull semen to improve milk yield and breed quality over time. A paid add-on option (gender-sorted semen) skews the odds heavily toward female calves, which is valuable for dairy farmers who specifically want more milking animals rather than males.
eligibility_text: Available to cattle-owning farmers in most Tamil Nadu districts, including Chennai, Coimbatore, Cuddalore, Erode, Kanchipuram, Kanyakumari, Krishnagiri, Madurai, Nagapattinam, Namakkal, Perambalur, Pudukkottai, Ramanathapuram, Ranipet, Salem, Sivagangai, Thanjavur, The Nilgiris, Thiruvallur, Thiruvannamalai, Tiruchirapalli, Tirunelveli, Thirupathur, Thoothukudi, Vellore, Villupuram and Virudhunagar. Check with your local AI centre to confirm current coverage.
documents_required: No specific document list was published on the official source checked — contact your local AI centre or Village Animal Husbandry Assistant with basic cattle ownership details to enrol
how_to_apply: Contact your nearest Artificial Insemination (AI) centre, Village Animal Husbandry Assistant, or veterinary hospital to request the service for your cattle.
fee: Standard AI service is free. The optional sex-sorted semen add-on costs ₹175 for the first insemination and ₹150 for a second attempt if needed.
processing_time: Service is typically provided on request at the farmer's location
helpline: Local Animal Husbandry / Veterinary office, or the Tamil Nadu Livestock Development Agency (TNLDA)

name: Saving-cum-Relief Scheme for Marine Fishermen (Fishing Ban Period)
department: Fisheries Department, Government of Tamil Nadu, under the central National Scheme of Welfare of Fishermen
introduced: Implemented in Tamil Nadu as part of the central National Scheme of Welfare of Fishermen; the state's per-family relief amount was raised from ₹2,000 to ₹5,000 in 2017 — exact original launch year in Tamil Nadu not independently confirmed.
summary: ₹5,000 in direct financial relief for marine fishermen crew/laborer families during the annual fishing ban period, when boats can't go out and there's no catch income.
about: Tamil Nadu enforces an annual fishing ban of about 61 days on the East Coast (roughly mid-April to end-May) to let fish stocks recover. This scheme gives registered marine fishermen — especially crew and laborers who have no other steady income during the ban — a direct cash relief payment, transferred straight to their bank account.
eligibility_text: You should be a registered marine fisherman working as crew or a laborer on a fishing boat, without another steady source of income during the ban period. Contribution to the savings component (where applicable) and cooperative society membership can factor into eligibility — confirm current terms with your local Fisheries Department office.
documents_required: Bank account passbook (Aadhaar-linked, for NEFT transfer)
Proof of engagement as boat crew/labor (from your cooperative society or boat owner)
how_to_apply: Register with your local Fisheries Department office or fishermen's cooperative society ahead of the ban period; the relief amount is credited directly to your bank account via NEFT after enrolment is verified.
fee: None to receive the relief; a savings contribution may apply depending on the specific scheme component
processing_time: Typically disbursed during or shortly after the fishing ban period, once registration is verified
helpline: Local Assistant Director of Fisheries office

name: Group Accident Insurance Scheme for Fisherfolk
department: Fisheries Department, Government of Tamil Nadu, under the centrally-sponsored National Scheme of Welfare of Fishermen
introduced: Run as part of the central, centrally-sponsored National Scheme of Welfare of Fishermen; exact Tamil Nadu launch date not independently confirmed.
summary: Free accident insurance for all registered fisherfolk — up to ₹2,00,000 if a fisherman dies, goes missing, or is permanently disabled at sea, with no premium to pay.
about: Covers marine and inland fisherfolk against accidental death, disappearance at sea, and disability. Because it's centrally sponsored, the fisherman doesn't pay any premium — the cost is borne by the government.
eligibility_text: Available to registered fisherfolk (marine and inland). No premium is collected from the fisherman under this centrally-sponsored scheme.
benefit_highlights: Partial disability: ₹1,00,000, plus ₹10,000 towards hospitalisation costs
No premium payable by the fisherman
documents_required: For a claim: death/disability certificate and supporting medical or police records (exact claim document list not independently confirmed — check with your local Fisheries office)
how_to_apply: Enrolment happens automatically when you register as a fisherman with the Fisheries Department or your local fishermen's cooperative society — there's no separate application for the insurance itself. Claims are filed through your local Assistant Director of Fisheries office.
fee: None — premium is fully paid by the government
processing_time: Not specified by source — claims are handled through the local Fisheries office
helpline: Local Assistant Director of Fisheries office
